content.title: Research use case
content.body: Define the decisions the platform should support: keyword prioritization, competitor discovery, content planning, technical auditing or reporting. Use a fixed list of target queries and domains so results can be compared consistently across tools.

content.title: Validate data coverage
content.body: Compare returned keywords, URLs, links and site issues with known examples and available first-party data. Record missing results, differences in definitions and the effort required to turn output into a client recommendation. Treat third-party traffic estimates as estimates, not audited facts.

content.title: Site auditing and reporting
content.body: Run a crawl on a controlled site and review whether issues are accurate, prioritized and actionable. Check crawl limits, exclusions, scheduling, exports and how changes are tracked over time. Test a report using the format and level of explanation a client actually needs.

content.title: Team and integration fit
content.body: Verify seats, permissions, project limits, export formats, API access and integration requirements in current documentation. Check whether the team can separate client data and remove access when a staff member leaves.

content.title: Pricing and decision
content.body: Ask for a dated quote using the same users, projects, tracked keywords, crawl volume and reporting needs. Include training, manual cleanup and duplicate tools. Current prices and plan limits are not independently verified in this review.

content.title: Pilot acceptance criteria
content.body: Choose a known website, a small set of target queries and a recurring client report. Have an analyst complete keyword research, inspect a technical crawl, export findings and explain the next action to a colleague. Record data gaps, manual cleanup and time needed to create a usable deliverable.

content.title: Failure cases and data interpretation
content.body: Check whether the tool's estimated metrics disagree with first-party analytics and why. Verify crawl exclusions, duplicate URLs, localization and canonical behavior. Keep a note of metric definitions and do not present third-party estimates as exact traffic, revenue or search-console results.

content.title: Decision record
content.body: Record the markets and languages required, number of users and projects, crawl needs, report recipients, exports and integrations. Compare only current plan details confirmed by the vendor. Revisit the choice if the agency changes service mix or the team cannot turn the data into actionable recommendations.

faqs.question: Who should evaluate Semrush?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Semrush when its primary workflow matches a documented requirement. Test a representative task and verify current capabilities and limits directly with the vendor.

faqs.question: How should a team test Semrush?
faqs.answer: Use the same real input, expected outcome and acceptance criteria each time. Record pass, partial pass, fail or unknown, including setup time, manual work and failure handling.

faqs.question: Which limitations should be checked in Semrush?
faqs.answer: Check the exact plan, integrations, permissions, export, data retention, recovery and ongoing administration. Treat untested or undocumented capabilities as unknown until confirmed.

faqs.question: Are Semrush prices and ratings independently verified here?
faqs.answer: No. Current prices, plan limits and independent ratings are not verified in this review. Check official documentation and obtain a dated quote before purchase.

faqs.question: What should be confirmed before adopting Semrush?
faqs.answer: Confirm the core workflow, access controls, integrations, data export, account offboarding, support responsibilities and renewal terms. Assign an owner for the implementation and ongoing review.
